title: Cap. IX Arg. 4 Sol cont.: Bellarmine's mediate/immediate dodge — sufficient help for an Indian or American infant in the parents cannot be explained
latin: Secundo, Bellarminus cogitur confugere ad illam distinctionem, mediate vel immediate; nec audet sustinere sufficientem gratiam omnibus parvulis immediate dari. At quam hoc obscurum est, huic parvulo, inter Indos aut Americanos nato, in parentibus suis fuisse exhibitum auxilium sufficiens, cum quale hoc fuerit, nemo potest explicare! Porro, si ad defensionem sufficientis gratiae liceat ad majores confugere, multo tutius et certius est ad primos usque parentes ascendere, de quibus nulla quaestio est, quin sufficientem gratiam in illis et posteri acceperint, quam in aliis majoribus nostris quibuscunque subsistere, de quibus incertum erit acceperintne talem sufficientem gratiam filiorum suorum nomine, an non acceperint.
pass_a: Secondly, Bellarmine is compelled to flee unto that distinction, mediate or immediate; nor does he dare to maintain that sufficient grace is immediately given unto all little ones. But how obscure this is — that unto this little one, born among the Indians or Americans, sufficient help was exhibited in his parents, when what sort this was, no one can explain! Further, if for the defense of sufficient grace it be lawful to flee unto ancestors, it is much safer and more certain to ascend even unto the first parents, concerning whom there is no question but that posterity also received sufficient grace in them, than to rest in any other of our ancestors whatsoever, concerning whom it will be uncertain whether they received such sufficient grace in the name of their children, or did not receive it.
pass_b: Second: Bellarmine is driven to the mediate-or-immediate distinction, and will not dare claim sufficient grace is given immediately to every infant. How dark that is — that an infant born among Indians or Americans had sufficient help shown in his parents, when no one can say what that help was! And if defending sufficient grace means fleeing to ancestors, it is far safer to go all the way back to the first parents — where no one doubts posterity also received sufficient grace in them — than to stop at any later ancestors, of whom it remains uncertain whether they received such sufficient grace in their children's name or not.

lemmas.gloss: Bellarmine will not grant immediate sufficient grace to all infants
obscure what sufficient help in pagan parents means

title: Cap. IX Arg. 4 Sol cont.: many adults lack immediate aid to believe — Bellarmine's 'posse' via creatures is a miserable defense of esse
latin: Denique inter ipsos adultos quamplurimi sunt, fatente Bellarmino, ibid. c. 8. quibus sufficiens auxilium ad credendum non immediate conceditur, sed hoc solummodo sensu concessum intelligitur, quia possunt cognoscere per creaturas Deum esse, et possunt a Deo excitari ad credendum quod Deus sit, et quod inquirentibus se remunerator sit; et possunt tali fide excitari ad orandum Deum, et hoc modo (quamvis destituantur praedicatione Evangelii) possunt impetrare ut vel ab ipso Deo, vel ab Angelo, vel ab aliquo homine in cognitione fidei illuminentur. Quam misera sit haec defensio, quae cum quaestio instituatur de esse, respondet solummodo de posse, non dubito quin omnes intelligatis. Eam solummodo obiter perstringere volui, ut videatis quam male fundata sit haec propositio de sufficiente gratia omnibus et singulis donata, quam disputatores nostri substernunt tanquam solidissimum fundamentum causae suae. Plura non addo, quia licet concedatur, non tamen facit ad solidam causae probationem, uti ab initio ostendimus.
pass_a: Finally among adults themselves very many there are, Bellarmine confessing, ibid. c. 8. unto whom sufficient help unto believing is not immediately granted, but is understood as granted only in this sense, that they can know through the creatures that God is, and can be stirred by God unto believing that God is, and that he is a rewarder unto them that seek him; and can by such faith be stirred unto praying unto God, and in this way (although destitute of the preaching of the Gospel) can obtain that they be illuminated in the knowledge of the faith either by God himself, or by an Angel, or by some man. How miserable this defense is, which when the question is instituted concerning being, answers only concerning being-able, I doubt not that you all understand. I wished only in passing to touch it, that you may see how ill founded is this proposition concerning sufficient grace given unto all and singular, which our disputers lay under as the most solid foundation of their cause. I add no more, because even if it be granted, it still does not make unto solid proof of the cause, as we showed from the beginning.
pass_b: Finally, among adults themselves, Bellarmine admits (ibid. c. 8), very many are not given immediate sufficient help to believe — only in this thin sense: they can know God through the creatures, can be stirred to believe that God is and rewards seekers, can be stirred by that faith to pray, and so (even without Gospel preaching) can obtain illumination in the faith from God, an angel, or some man. Miserable defense: the question is about what is, and the answer is only about what can be — you all see that. I touch it only in passing, to show how poorly founded is the claim that sufficient grace is given to every person, which our disputers lay as their cause's firmest base. I add nothing more: even if granted, it still does not solidly prove their cause, as we showed from the start.

lemmas.gloss: Bellarmine: many adults only 'can' know God via creatures
question of being answered with mere possibility

title: Cap. IX Arg. A vocatione Evangelica: absolute antecedent election/reprobation would make indiscriminate Gospel offers a simulation — therefore reprobation only after foresight of despised grace
latin: A vocatione Evangelica sic disputant. Si Deus decreto antecedaneo et absoluto quosdam elegisset, quosdam reprobasset, ageret simulate gratiam offerendo hominibus indiscriminatim per ministros evangelicos. Nam neque precise ad salutem electis mandari potest ut credant sub spe salutis adipiscendae; quia nemo sub conditione exspectat, quod sibi scit absolute ordinatum: neque reprobatis mandari potest ut credant; nam Deus sic exigeret ab eis ut falsum crederent, scilicet Christum pro illis fuisse passum et mortuum, illisque vitam et reconciliationem impetrasse. Ergo statuendum est, neminem reprobari nisi ex consideratione et praevisione spretae gratiae, et finalis permansionis in hac cordis obduratione et infidelitate.
pass_a: From the Evangelical vocation they so dispute. If God by an antecedent and absolute decree had elected some, reprobated some, he would act with simulation in offering grace indiscriminately unto men through evangelical ministers. For neither can it be commanded precisely unto the elect unto salvation that they believe under hope of obtaining salvation; because no one under a condition expects that which he knows to be absolutely ordained unto himself: nor can it be commanded unto the reprobate that they believe; for God would so exact of them that they believe a falsehood, namely that Christ suffered and died for them, and obtained life and reconciliation for them. Therefore it is to be established that no one is reprobated except from consideration and foresight of despised grace, and of final continuance in this obduration of heart and unbelief.
pass_b: From the Gospel call they argue thus. If God by an antecedent absolute decree had elected some and reprobated others, he would be acting with simulation when he offers grace indiscriminately through evangelical ministers. For the elect unto salvation cannot be commanded to believe under hope of obtaining salvation — no one awaits under a condition what he knows is absolutely ordained for him. Nor can the reprobate be commanded to believe — God would then require them to believe a falsehood: that Christ suffered and died for them and obtained life and reconciliation for them. Therefore, they say, no one is reprobated except from regard and foresight of despised grace and final persistence in that hardness of heart and unbelief.

lemmas.gloss: adversaries: absolute reprobation makes indiscriminate offers simulation
reprobation only after foresight of despised grace

title: Cap. IX Sol: reprobation here means fixed decree not to give special efficacious grace — damnation from sin; denial of that grace from mere liberty of will
latin: Hic in memoriam revocandum est, quod subinde cogimur repetere, nos, per reprobationem, quam ex mera Dei voluntate et non ex praevisis demeritis humanis suspendimus, intelligere, non peremptorium decretum damnandi, vel morte aeterna afficiendi singularem aliquam personam, sed fixum decretum non-impertiendi specialem illam et efficacem gratiam, sive vocationem secundum propositum, absque qua Deus videt hanc singularem personam in sua duritia, impoenitentia, et infidelitate permansuram, atque decrevit illud permittere. Est quidem Deo certissimum, ex tali praeteritione hominem sic rejectum in peccatis suis moriturum: Est etiam Deo decretissimum, eundem hominem damnare propter peccata illa in quibus morietur: interim tamen haud obscurum est, negationem talis gratiae (in qua reprobationem proprie sitam esse putamus) ex mera libertate Divinae voluntatis pendere, at damnationem talis personae ex peccato ejusdem oriri.
pass_a: Here it is to be called back unto memory, what we are from time to time compelled to repeat, that we, by reprobation, which we hang from the mere will of God and not from foresighted human demerits, understand not a peremptory decree of damning, or of afflicting with eternal death, some singular person, but a fixed decree of not imparting that special and efficacious grace, or vocation according to purpose, without which God sees that this singular person will remain in his hardness, impenitence, and unbelief, and has decreed to permit that. It is indeed most certain unto God, that from such passing-by the man so rejected will die in his sins: It is also most decreed unto God to damn the same man on account of those sins in which he will die: yet meanwhile it is not obscure that the denial of such grace (in which we think reprobation is properly situated) hangs from the mere liberty of the Divine will, but that the damnation of such a person arises from his own sin.
pass_b: Recall again what we must keep repeating: by reprobation — which we hang from God's mere will, not from foresighted human demerits — we do not mean a peremptory decree to damn or eternally afflict some particular person, but a fixed decree not to impart that special efficacious grace, or calling according to purpose, without which God sees that person will remain in hardness, impenitence, and unbelief — and has decreed to permit that. God is most certain that from such passing-over the man so rejected will die in his sins, and most decided to damn him for those sins in which he will die. Yet it is plain: denial of that grace (where we locate reprobation properly) hangs on mere liberty of divine will, while that person's damnation arises from his own sin.

lemmas.gloss: reprobation = decree not to give special efficacious grace
damnation from sin; grace-denial from free will

title: Cap. IX Sol: without simulation God can offer remission and life indiscriminately on condition of faith — reprobation decree is not 'even if Judas believes he will not be saved'
latin: Hisce praelibatis respondeo, Deum absque omni simulatione, non obstante tali decreto reprobationis, posse per evangelicos ministros remissionem peccatorum et vitam aeternam hominibus indiscriminatim proponere sub conditione hac, Si crediderint in Christum. Neque simulat Deus quando sub hac conditione promittit salutem promiscue quibusvis hominibus, quia cuivis homini conditionem implenti promissum beneficium fideliter exhibebit. Si reprobationis decretum in hanc formam conciperetur, Etiamsi Judas crediderit, non obtinebit remissionem peccatorum, aut vitam aeternam, esset manifesta illusio quoad reprobatos in praedicatione Evangelii. Sed illud decretum hoc tantum continet, Non dabo Judae specialem illam gratiam, qua mediante conditionem propositam de facto impleret. Si Deum simulationis velint coarguere, ostendere debent, Deum promisisse per ministros evangelicos se daturum hanc specialem gratiam alicui personae, quam nihilominus antecedaneo reprobationis decreto ab eadem rejecit. Hoc si fecerint, quod nunquam facere poterunt, nos (quod absit) Deum simulationis peragi ab illis reum patiemur.
pass_a: These things having been first tasted, I answer that God without any simulation, such a decree of reprobation notwithstanding, can through evangelical ministers propose remission of sins and eternal life indiscriminately unto men under this condition, If they shall have believed in Christ. Nor does God simulate when under this condition he promises salvation promiscuously unto any men whatsoever, because unto any man fulfilling the condition he will faithfully exhibit the promised benefit. If the decree of reprobation were conceived in this form, Even if Judas shall have believed, he will not obtain remission of sins, or eternal life, there would be a manifest illusion as to the reprobate in the preaching of the Gospel. But that decree contains only this, I will not give unto Judas that special grace by means of which he would in fact fulfill the condition proposed. If they wish to convict God of simulation, they ought to show that God promised through evangelical ministers that he would give this special grace unto some person, whom nonetheless by an antecedent decree of reprobation he rejected from the same. If they shall have done this, which they will never be able to do, we (which God forbid) will suffer God to be prosecuted by them as guilty of simulation.
pass_b: With that premise I answer: reprobation decree notwithstanding, God can without any simulation, through evangelical ministers, set before men indiscriminately remission of sins and eternal life on this condition — If they believe in Christ. Nor does he simulate when under that condition he promises salvation to any whatsoever: to whoever fulfills the condition he will faithfully give the promised benefit. If the reprobation decree were cast as Even if Judas believes, he will not obtain remission or eternal life, Gospel preaching to the reprobate would be open illusion. But that decree holds only this: I will not give Judas that special grace by which he would in fact fulfill the proposed condition. To convict God of simulation they must show he promised through evangelical ministers to give that special grace to someone whom he nonetheless rejected from it by antecedent reprobation. If they ever do that — which they never can — we will (God forbid) let them prosecute God as guilty of simulation.

lemmas.gloss: indiscriminate offer under faith-condition is no simulation
decree withholds special grace, not voids conditional promise

title: Cap. IX Sol: willing to save anyone if he believes is not decreeing to work faith in everyone — Remonstrants confuse the two; conditional will = faith-salvation nexus
latin: Intelligant itaque Remonstrantes, qui hoc passim urgent, aliud esse velle serio quemlibet hominem servare si credat, aliud decernere operari in quolibet homine ut credat. Potest Deus velle prius absque omni simulatione, quamvis quoad quosdam decreverit nolle posterius in illorum reprobatione. Hic tamen in transcursu illud monere haud abs re erit, cum dicimus Deum velle servare quemlibet hominem si credat, nos nihil aliud denotare per hanc conditionatam voluntatem, quam aeternam illam et inviolabilem Dei ordinationem de nexu indissolubili fidei et salutis: propter quem nexum de qualibet persona electa vel non-electa verificatur haec promissio, Si credideris, salvus eris. Interim voluntas Dei non intelligitur versari circa salutem hominis non-electi quasi suspensa aut incerta; sed hujusmodi loquendi formulis id affirmatur, si conditio fidei in objecto poneretur, esset etiam in Deo voluntas actualis talem personam servandi: quod sufficit ad excludendam illam simulationem quam Deo impingere conantur.
pass_a: Let the Remonstrants therefore understand, who everywhere urge this, that it is one thing seriously to will to save any man if he believe, another to decree to work in any man that he believe. God can will the former without any simulation, although as to some he has decreed not to will the latter in their reprobation. Here nevertheless in passing it will not be beside the point to warn, when we say that God wills to save any man if he believe, that we denote by this conditioned will nothing other than that eternal and inviolable ordination of God concerning the indissoluble nexus of faith and salvation: on account of which nexus this promise is verified of any elect or non-elect person, If thou shalt have believed, thou shalt be saved. Meanwhile the will of God is not understood to be conversant about the salvation of the non-elect man as if suspended or uncertain; but by such forms of speaking this is affirmed, that if the condition of faith were posited in the object, there would also be in God an actual will of saving such a person: which suffices unto excluding that simulation which they endeavor to fasten upon God.
pass_b: So let the Remonstrants, who press this everywhere, understand: it is one thing seriously to will to save anyone if he believes, another to decree to work in anyone so that he believes. God can will the first without any simulation, even while for some he has decreed not to will the second in their reprobation. One passing note: when we say God wills to save anyone if he believes, by that conditioned will we mean only God's eternal inviolable ordination of the indissoluble bond of faith and salvation — for which bond the promise If you believe, you will be saved holds true of any elect or non-elect person. God's will is not thereby pictured as hanging uncertain over a non-elect man's salvation; such speech only affirms that if the faith-condition were set in the object, God would also actually will to save that person — enough to shut out the simulation they try to pin on God.

lemmas.lemma: servare si credat / operari ut credat
lemmas.gloss: conditional save-will ≠ decree to work faith in all
